data.name: Khawwas
data.gender_notes: Khawwas is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'khawwana' meaning 'to know', 'to be knowledgeable', or 'to be wise'. In Islamic tradition, Khawwas is a name for those who possess deep knowledge and understanding of the faith. The name Khawwas carries the meaning “Wise, Knowledgeable” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Khawwas usually hope their child will grow to embody wise, knowledgeable and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes wisdom, knowledge, and understanding in the path of Islam.
data.etymology: Khawwas belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Wise, Knowledgeable.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Khawwas total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_arabic.name: خَوَّاس
in_arabic.long_meaning: خَوَّاس هو اسم عربي يعود إلى الجذر خ و س، والذي يعني المراقبة أو الحفاظ، وله استخدامات تاريخية في الإسلام كمراقب أو حارس للمسجد أو الأملاك، ويعتبر من الأسماء الفريدة التي تحمل معاني روحية عميقة في الثقافة الإسلامية

in_urdu.name: خَوَّاس
in_urdu.long_meaning: خَوَّاس ایک عربی نام ہے جو خ و س کے gốc سے اخذ ہوا ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے نگرانی یا حفاظت، اور اس کا استعمال اسلامی تاریخ میں مسجد یا املاک کے نگران یا محافظ کے طور پر ہوا ہے، اور یہ نام جنوبی ایشیائی مسلم روایت میں روحانی اہمیت کا حامل ہے

in_hindi.name: ख़व्वास
in_hindi.long_meaning: ख़व्वास एक अरबी नाम है जो ख और व के मूल से लिया गया है, जिसका अर्थ है रक्षक या संरक्षक, और इसका उपयोग इस्लामी इतिहास में मस्जिद या संपत्ति के रक्षक या संरक्षक के रूप में हुआ है, और यह नाम भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में आध्यात्मिक महत्व को धारण करता है

in_pashto.name: خَوَّاس
in_pashto.long_meaning: خَوَّاس د عربی نوم دی چې د خ و س څخه اخیستل شوی، چې د ساتونکي یا ساتندوی په معنی دی، او دا نوم د اسلامي تاریخ په دوران کې د مسجد یا ملکیت د ساتونکي یا ساتندوی په توګه کارول شوی دی، او دا نوم په افغان/پښتون دود کې د روحاني महतوبو درلودونکی دی

historical_references.reference: Ibn Abd al-Hakam, Futuh al-Buldan. Translated by H.V. Morton. Philadelphia: University of Pennsylvania Press, 1937.
historical_references.context: Khawwas ibn Thabit al-Khawwas was a Berber general who served under the Fatimid Caliph al-Mu'izz li-din Allah (r. 953-975). He played a crucial role in the Fatimid conquest of Egypt, defeating the Ikhshidid forces at the Battle of al-Fim and securing Egypt for the Fatimid Caliphate.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Khaldun, The History of the Berbers. Translated by Peter R. Lamborn and James T. Monroe. Princeton: Princeton University Press, 1958.
historical_references.context: Khawwas ibn Al-Husayn Al-Masri was a prominent figure in the Hafsid state of Tunisia in the 14th century. He was a military commander and an influential advisor to the Hafsid rulers. Khawwas is best known for his role in the Hafsid conquest of Constantine, where he led the final assault on the city and secured it for the Hafsids.
